Jamie takes out an interest-free loan of £8100
Jamie makes a payment every month to pay back the loan.
Jamie repays £400 in month 1, £390 in month 2, £380 in month 3, and so on, so that the
amounts repaid each month form an arithmetic sequence.

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text: Show that Jamie repays £290 in month 12

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
After Jamie’s Nth payment, the loan is completely paid back.
Show that \( N^2 - 81N + 1620 = 0 \)

questions.label: (c)
questions.question_text: Hence find the value of \( N \).

The point P(3, -2) lies on the curve with equation y = f(x), x ∈ ℝ

Find the coordinates of the point to which P is mapped when the curve with
equation y = f(x) is transformed to the curve with equation

(i) y = f(x - 2)

(ii) y = f(2x)

(iii) y = 3f(-x) + 5

A sequence u_1, u_2, u_3, ... is defined by

u_{n+1} = ku_n - 5
u_1 = 6

where k is a positive constant.

Given that u_3 = -1

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text:
show that

6k^2 - 5k - 4 = 0

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
Hence

(i) find the value of k,

(ii) find the value of \sum_{r=1}^{3} u_r.

θ tan 2θ

 \( f(x) = e^{4x^2 - 1}  x > 0 \)
 \( g(x) = 8 ln x  x > 0 \)

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
Given that f'(x) = g'(x) at x = α
show that α satisfies the equation
4x² + 2 ln x − 1 = 0

The iterative formula

\( x_{n+1} = \sqrt{\frac{1 - 2 \ln x_n}{4}} \) 

is used with \( x_1 = 0.6 \) to find an approximate value for α
Calculate, giving each answer to 4 decimal places,
(i) the value of x_2
(ii) the value of α

Relative to a fixed origin O

questions.label: (a)

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text:
Prove that

\( \frac{1}{\csc \theta - 1} + \frac{1}{\csc \theta + 1} \equiv 2 \tan \theta \sec \theta \)

\( \theta \neq (90n)^\circ , \ n \in \mathbb{Z} \)

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
Hence solve, for \( 0 < x < 90^\circ \), the equation

\( \frac{1}{\csc 2x - 1} + \frac{1}{\csc 2x + 1} = \cot 2x \sec 2x \)

Give each answer, in degrees, to one decimal place.

The graph in Figure 3 shows the path of a small ball.
The ball travels in a vertical plane above horizontal ground.
The ball is thrown from the point represented by A and caught at the point represented by B.
The height, H metres, of the ball above the ground has been plotted against the horizontal distance, x metres, measured from the point where the ball was thrown.
With respect to a fixed origin O, the point A has coordinates (0, 2) and the point B has
coordinates (20, 0.8), as shown in Figure 3.
The ball reaches its maximum height when x = 9
A quadratic function, linking H with x, is used to model the path of the ball.

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text: Find H in terms of x.

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text: Give one limitation of the model.

questions.label: (c)
questions.question_text:
Chandra is standing directly under the path of the ball at a point 16m horizontally
from O.
Chandra can catch the ball if the ball is less than 2.5 m above the ground.
Use the model to determine if Chandra can catch the ball.

Figure 4 shows a sketch of the curve C with parametric equations

x = (t + 3)^2    y = 1 - t^3    -2 ≤ t ≤ 1

The point P with coordinates (4, 2) lies on C.

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text:
Using parametric differentiation, show that the tangent to C at P has equation

3x + 4y = 20

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
The curve C is used to model the profile of a slide at a water park.
Units are in metres, with y being the height of the slide above water level.

Find, according to the model, the greatest height of the slide above water level.

In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.

Figure 5 shows a sketch of part of the curve C with equation

y = 8x^2 e^{-3x}    x ≥ 0

The finite region R, shown shaded in Figure 5, is bounded by
• the curve C
• the line with equation x = 1
• the x-axis

Find the exact area of R, giving your answer in the form

A + Be^{-3}

where A and B are rational numbers to be found.

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text: Express \( \frac{1}{V(25 - V)} \) in partial fractions.

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
The volume, \( V \) microlitres, of a plant cell \( t \) hours after the plant is watered is modelled by the differential equation
\[ \frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{1}{10} V (25 - V) \]
The plant cell has an initial volume of 20 microlitres.
Find, according to the model, the time taken, in minutes, for the volume of the plant cell to reach 24 microlitres.

questions.label: (c)
questions.question_text:
Show that
 \[ V = \frac{A}{e^{-kt} + B} \]
where \( A, B \text{ and } k \) are constants to be found.

questions.label: (d)
questions.question_text:
The model predicts that there is an upper limit, \( L \) microlitres, on the volume of the plant cell.
Find the value of \( L \), giving a reason for your answer.

The world human population, P billions, is modelled by the equation

P = ab^t

where a and b are constants and t is the number of years after 2004

Using the estimated population figures for the years from 2004 to 2007, a graph is plotted of log10 P against t.

The points lie approximately on a straight line with

• gradient 0.0054
• intercept 0.81 on the log10 P axis

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text: Estimate, to 3 decimal places, the value of a and the value of b.

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
(i) interpret the value of the constant a,

(ii) interpret the value of the constant b.

questions.label: (c)
questions.question_text: Use the model to estimate the world human population in 2030

questions.label: (d)
questions.question_text: Comment on the reliability of the answer to part (c).

The circle \( C_1 \) has equation
 \( x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 14y + 33 = 0 \)

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text:
Find
(i) the coordinates of the centre of \( C_1 \)
(ii) the radius of \( C_1 \)

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
A different circle \( C_2 \)
• has centre with coordinates (−6, −8)
• has radius \( k \), where \( k \) is a constant

Given that \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \) intersect at 2 distinct points,
find the range of values of \( k \), writing your answer in set notation.

The curve C has equation

(x + y)^3 = 3x^2 - 3y - 2

questions.label: (a)
questions.question_text:
Find an expression for 
\( \frac{dy}{dx} \) in terms of x and y.

questions.label: (b)
questions.question_text:
The point P(1, 0) lies on C.
Show that the normal to C at P has equation

y = -2x + 2

questions.label: (c)
questions.question_text:
Prove that the normal to C at P does not meet C again.

You should use algebra for your proof and make your reasoning clear.
